intro.title: Build end to end capstone production ready commerce backend Node
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a complete, production-ready e-commerce backend using Node.js. You'll learn to create RESTful APIs for managing products, orders, and users, applying core programming concepts like routing, middleware, and data validation. The main technologies involved are Express.js for the server framework, MongoDB for the database, and JWT for authentication. By the end, you'll have a functional backend that handles real-world commerce operations, giving you hands-on experience with essential Node.js development skills.
intro.usecase: This capstone project mirrors the backend architecture of real-world e-commerce platforms like Shopify, Amazon, or custom storefronts. You'll build production-ready APIs that handle critical operations such as product inventory management, user authentication, shopping cart sessions, and secure payment processing. As a backend developer, you'll implement scalable database models, middleware for security and logging, and RESTful endpoints that frontend applications consume. These skills are directly applicable to creating robust commerce backends for retail websites, mobile shopping apps, or B2B marketplaces where reliability and performance are essential.

objectives: Construct a RESTful API server using Express.js to handle HTTP requests and responses.
Configure a MongoDB database connection and define schemas for product and order data.
Implement CRUD operations for managing product inventory and processing customer orders.
Integrate user authentication middleware to secure API endpoints and control access.
Apply input validation and error handling to ensure data integrity and graceful failure.
Initialize and configure environment variables for managing different deployment settings.
Render API documentation to describe available endpoints and their expected behaviors.

steps.title: Import Express and required middleware
steps.instruction: Import Express, body-parser, and cors to handle HTTP requests and middleware.
steps.hint: Use require() statements to import these Node.js packages.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express, body-parser, and cors here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express framework and essential middleware packages are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Express, body-parser, and cors are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some packages, but make sure to import Express, body-parser, AND cors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or missing. You need to import Express, body-parser, and cors using require().

steps.title: Initialize Express application
steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance and assign it to a constant variable named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the Express import you already have to create the app instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an Express app instance
const app = express();

steps.expectedOutcome: The Express application is initialized and ready to be configured.
successCriteria: An Express app instance is created and assigned to a constant variable named 'app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating the Express app instance using the imported express function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Express app instance wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using the imported express function to create the app.

steps.title: Configure middleware
steps.instruction: Add middleware to your Express app to parse JSON request bodies and enable CORS.
steps.hint: Use app.use() to add the body-parser.json() middleware and the cors() middleware.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will be configured to parse JSON request bodies and handle cross-origin requests.
successCriteria: The app uses body-parser.json() and cors() middleware via app.use().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some middleware, but make sure to include both body-parser.json() and cors().
steps.feedbackWrong: The middleware configuration is missing or incorrect. Use app.use() to add both body-parser.json() and cors().

steps.title: Create in-memory product data store
steps.instruction: Define an array of product objects with id, name, price, and description properties. Place this array after the middleware configuration.
steps.hint: Create a constant variable named 'products' and assign it an array containing at least one product object with the required properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a 'products' array containing at least one product object with id, name, price, and description properties.
successCriteria: A 'products' array is defined with at least one object containing id, name, price, and description properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have an array named 'products' with at least one object containing id, name, price, and description properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The product data store wasn't created correctly. You need to define an array named 'products' with objects containing id, name, price, and description properties.

steps.title: Create GET endpoint to fetch all products
steps.instruction: Create a GET route at '/api/products' that returns all products from the products array.
steps.hint: Use app.get() to define the route. The route handler should send the products array as JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET endpoint is created that responds with all products when accessing '/api/products'.
successCriteria: The endpoint is defined with app.get('/api/products', ...) and returns the products array as JSON.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.get() with the correct route path and returning the products array as JSON.
steps.feedbackWrong: The endpoint isn't quite right. Check that you're using app.get() with '/api/products' and sending the products array as JSON response.

steps.title: Create GET endpoint to fetch single product
steps.instruction: Add a GET route at '/api/products/:id' that returns a specific product by ID from the products array. Use req.params.id to get the ID and find the matching product.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the route path containing ':id' as a parameter. Inside the handler, convert req.params.id to a number and use Array.find() to locate the product.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new route '/api/products/:id' is added that returns a single product object when a valid ID is provided, or a 404 error if not found.
successCriteria: Route uses app.get() with '/api/products/:id', extracts req.params.id, converts it to a number, finds the product with Array.find(), returns the product as JSON for success, and returns a 404 JSON error for missing products.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that you're using req.params.id, converting it to a number, and handling both success (200) and not-found (404) cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The endpoint isn't working as expected. Make sure you're using app.get() with the correct route path, extracting the ID parameter, and returning appropriate JSON responses.

steps.title: Create POST endpoint to add new product
steps.instruction: Create a POST route at '/api/products' that adds a new product to the products array. The route should extract name and price from the request body, generate a new id, and push the new product object to the array.
steps.hint: Use app.post() with the route path '/api/products'. In the handler, create a new product object with an id (you can use products.length + 1), name, and price from req.body, then push it to the products array and send back the new product as JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST endpoint at '/api/products' that successfully adds new products to the in-memory store and returns the created product with a 201 status.
successCriteria: POST route '/api/products' is created, extracts name and price from req.body, generates a new id, pushes the new product to the products array, and returns the new product as JSON.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your endpoint extracts both name and price from req.body, generates a proper id, and pushes the complete product object to the array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint is missing or incomplete. Make sure to create app.post('/api/products', ...) with a handler that creates a new product object and adds it to the products array.

steps.title: Create PUT endpoint to update existing product
steps.instruction: Create a PUT route at '/api/products/:id' that updates an existing product. Use req.params.id to find the product and req.body to get the updated data.
steps.hint: Use app.put() with the route path. Find the product index by id, then update that product's properties with the new data from req.body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PUT endpoint that can update product details by ID, returning the updated product or a 404 error if not found.
successCriteria: PUT route at '/api/products/:id' is defined, finds product by id, updates with req.body data, and returns appropriate JSON response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your route uses app.put(), finds the product by id, and updates it with the data from req.body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PUT endpoint isn't quite right. Check the route path, how you find the product, and how you update its properties.

steps.title: Create DELETE endpoint to remove product
steps.instruction: Create a DELETE route at '/api/products/:id' that removes a product from the products array based on the id parameter. Use findIndex to locate the product and splice to remove it, returning a 404 if the product is not found.
steps.hint: Remember to parse the id parameter to a number, find the index, and if found, remove the element with splice. Send appropriate status codes and messages.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DELETE endpoint is added that successfully removes a product by id from the products array and handles missing products with a 404 response.
successCriteria: The DELETE route '/api/products/:id' is defined, uses findIndex and splice to remove the product, and returns appropriate JSON responses with correct status codes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're correctly parsing the id, finding the index, and handling the 404 case.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DELETE endpoint is missing or incorrect. Ensure you define the route, remove the product from the array, and handle not-found cases.

steps.title: Start the server and test endpoints
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000 with a console log message.
steps.hint: Use app.listen() to start the server on port 3000 and provide a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start and be ready to handle requests on port 3000.
successCriteria: app.listen() is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't starting correctly. You need to call app.listen() with port 3000 and provide a callback that logs a message.
